usage.notes: Use CELLxGENE Census for targeted, version-pinned single-cell slices and reproducible build-time summaries. The Census is designed for server/cloud-scale access; Panacea should query only the required organism/tissue/cell-type/gene subset and return compact normalized aggregates to the browser rather than loading whole Census matrices. Prefer a named/LTS Census release for scientific reproducibility instead of the moving latest alias.

license.identifier: Census code MIT; Census data CC BY
license.scope: The official CELLxGENE Census repository states that repository code is reusable under the MIT license and Census data are available for reuse under CC BY. Individual studies/datasets remain scientifically attributable to their original authors and should retain dataset-level citations even when accessed through Census.
license.notes: Cite CELLxGENE Census and preserve citations for each underlying study/dataset contributing materially to an analysis. Do not imply that CC BY Census availability removes scientific attribution obligations or licenses unrelated linked content.

validation.notes: Single-cell expression is research/reference evidence affected by tissue sampling, disease state, assay chemistry, sequencing depth, preprocessing, ontology annotation and study design. A Census cell annotation or expression value is not patient-specific anatomy, pathology or diagnosis and must not independently determine treatment.

provenance.authority: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative / CZ CELLxGENE Discover
provenance.notes: Persist the named Census data release/build, Census schema version, CELLxGENE dataset schema version, organism ontology ID, source dataset/collection ID and citation, tissue/tissue_general ontology IDs, cell-type ontology ID, disease ontology ID, assay ontology ID, donor/sample metadata used in the slice, feature/gene identifiers, measurement layer semantics, query/filter expression, retrieval date and Panacea adapter version. Census release version and Census schema version are separate concepts and must never be conflated.

adapter.notes: Planned flow: organ/tissue/cell/gene research query -> choose explicit stable/LTS Census release -> apply ontology-based SOMA slice server-side or in an isolated analysis worker -> retain dataset/study and ontology provenance -> compute only required deterministic summaries -> normalize to PanaceaSingleCellReference -> deliver compact aggregates/metadata to UI. Never treat author-normalized values from an unrelated study as directly comparable to raw counts from another study without a documented harmonization method. Do not silently merge cell types across ontology versions or disease contexts.

trust.notes: High-authority, versioned and ontology-rich single-cell corpus with strong reproducibility when Census release, schema and source datasets are pinned. Biological/technical heterogeneity across contributing studies remains substantial, so evidence quality is contextual rather than equivalent to a validated patient assay.
